purpose: Disprove the inference from finite individual objects or a finite object collection to a finite temporal history or a first temporal state.

interpretation.earlier_than: m < n in the usual integer order means state m is earlier than state n
interpretation.object_exists_at: a exists at every temporal state n in Z

verified_consequences.no_first_temporal_state: For every n in Z, n-1 is a temporal state and n-1 < n.
verified_consequences.no_finite_history_conclusion: The temporal-state set Z is infinite.

refutes: every object is finite -> temporal history is finite
the collection of objects is finite -> temporal history is finite
every object is finite -> a first temporal state exists
does_not_refute: the complete temporal-state set is finite and nonempty, with a strict total order -> a first state exists
the temporal order is well-founded -> a first state exists, assuming a nonempty state set and a strict total order
does_not_claim: that the physical universe has an infinite past
that this abstract model describes actual cosmology
that time is fundamental rather than emergent

proof_sketch: Let the object domain be the singleton {a}; it is finite.
Let temporal states be the integers Z with the usual strict order.
Let a exist at every integer-indexed state.
For any proposed first state n, the state n-1 exists and is earlier.
Therefore the history has no first state, despite the finite object domain and finite individual object.
next_missing_premise: An independently justified principle linking the intended notion of finiteness to well-foundedness of the global temporal order.
